column1: # The starting violation list of Broiler.RegEx's architecture tests: every violation that a rule SL1 to SL10 or a
# contract check C1, C3 or C5 of rules.register.json finds in the library on the day the tests were filed, 2026-10-25,
# at work package SJL-11.2 of the shared JavaScript libraries programme, at the code 0.1.0-preview.4 was packed from.
# Broiler.VM's JSD-0081 (section X3) lists the conventions these breach, and requirements R1 to R11 close them.
# Each rule's test asserts its rows in both directions: a violation the rule finds that is not here fails it, and so
# does a row the rule no longer finds. A change that removes a violation removes its row in the same change; no change
# adds one. SJL-11.2 shrinks the list to none, and bundle sjl-11-001's check E-3 holds it empty at the candidate reading.
# Where a rule reads where a violation is - SL1's assembly half, SL3, SL4 and C5 from the IL and the PDB's sequence
# points, SL5 from the NoWarn and WarningsNotAsErrors elements of the project and build files - its test asserts the
# row place by place as well: every place the rule finds is cited once, and every cited place is one the rule finds. A
# second call of a listed member is a new place and fails the test, and so does a citation left on a line that no
# longer holds the violation, although the row's wording is the same in both. Every other row's violation names its one
# place: a static field, a public member or type, a file, a package, a setting.
# Columns, tab-separated: the rule or check; the violation, exactly as the rule words it; a token the source holds where
# the violation is; and the places, path:line, space-separated, one line of each (a statement can span several).
# RuleRegisterTests checks that each cited line holds the token, so a citation moves with the code; the rule's own test
# decides whether the violation, and each place of it, is still there. A comment line here names a row's repair.
